In low-income countries private out-of-pocket pay-
ments account for more than half of the mere $2 to
$40 per person spent each year for health care.
Most of this sum goes for doctors' fees, payments
to traditional healers, and drugs. NGOs, particu-
larly those related to religious institutions, make
important contributions to the provision of health
services in many low-income countries. In Tan-
zania and Haiti NGOs operate nearly half of the
hospitals, and in Cameroon and Uganda they
manage 40 percent of health facilities. In Ghana
and Nigeria about a third of all hospital beds are
located in mission hospitals. Government spend-
